title: Tax Assessment Strategies
content: A comprehensive guide on various strategies employed during tax assessments for extended family members. This document outlines the general procedures and common practices, including a case study on a recent client, David Thompson, who is an extended family member. In 2022, David fell into the income bracket of $75,000 to $150,000. He was able to claim a deduction for his home office and educational expenses, which amounted to $5,000. After applying the standard deduction and personal exemptions, his taxable income was reduced to $65,000. The final tax liability, accounting for federal and state taxes, was calculated to be approximately $12,000.

title: Common Deductions and Credits
content: An overview of the most common tax deductions and credits available to taxpayers, specifically extended family members, which can significantly impact the outcome of a tax assessment. This includes deductions such as mortgage interest, educational expenses, and charitable donations. Tax credits discussed include the Earned Income Credit, Child Tax Credit, and Education Credits.

title: Tax Law Changes for 2022
content: Summary of the latest tax law changes that came into effect in 2022, which may affect tax assessments and returns for individuals and businesses, including extended family members. Key changes include adjustments to income tax brackets, increases in standard deduction amounts, and the expansion of certain tax credits.
